subject: System Design
title: The Slack Connectivity Crisis
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Slack Connectivity Crisis usable.

hook.text: On January 4, 2021, millions tried to log into Slack after New Year's. It couldn't handle the stampede.

buildup.text: Everyone returned to work on the same Monday morning, creating a massive simultaneous login spike.

discovery.text: Slack's infrastructure wasn't provisioned for the thundering herd of post-holiday reconnections.

twist.text: The problem wasn't total load — it was the spike pattern. Gradual load would have been fine.

climax.text: Thundering herd problems occur when many clients retry at the same time, amplifying the original spike.

punchline.text: Millions logging in at once can overwhelm any system.

quiz.question: What is a thundering herd problem?
options: Many clients retrying simultaneously amplify a spike
Too many servers processing at once
A database running out of storage
